From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kent <alex.kent@cloud-fabric.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Migration PoC — architecture review & final slot coordination

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. Per our conversation about running a focused PoC to validate performance and migration steps away from your EdgeScale self-hosted cluster, I'd like to schedule a 60–90 minute architecture deep-dive (we'll combine infra details + migration checklist + success criteria).

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue 2026-06-16 — 10:00–11:30
- Wed 2026-06-17 — 09:00–10:30
- Thu 2026-06-17 — 14:00–15:30

Agenda we plan to cover:
- Overview of current inference setup and bottlenecks
- Model compatibility and quantization constraints
- Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for your compliance needs
- Warmup/KV-cache strategies, batching, and rollback plan
- PoC success metrics and timeline

Please let me know which slot works and whether you want any specific Redwood engineers on the call. I attached a short PoC scope doc and a checklist we use in most migration PoCs.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer (Pre-sales)
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: PoC-scope.pdf
From: Alex Kent <alex.kent@cloud-fabric.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration PoC — architecture review & final slot coordination

Dev —

Thanks, appreciate the clear agenda. The team is keen on Wed but we have a hard conflict at 09:00 PT. Can we do Wed 09:30–11:00 PT instead? If not, Thu 14:00 PT also works.

A few quick notes from our side so you can prep:
- We're migrating from an EdgeScale self-hosted cluster running Triton + custom KV cache. Peak seq len varies a lot (64–2048 tokens).
- Models: a mix of OSS Llama-2-70B and a couple of in-house fine-tuned variants.
- Primary concerns: quantization artifacts, token-latency tail, and live rollback without losing traffic.

Adding Samir (Infra Lead) to this thread — he can drop a network diagram and the list of current GPUs. Attached the diagram and a short inventory.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Platform, Cloud Fabric
alex.kent@cloud-fabric.ai | +1 (212) 555-0199

Alex —

Thanks for the context and for adding Samir. Wed 09:30–11:00 PT works for us — I've penciled that slot. I've looped in Marissa (Solutions Engineering) to lead the technical deep-dive and Grace (AM) to cover commercial/governance items.

Prep for the call (quick asks so we can come ready):
- Samir: can you paste GPU types (model + driver), network NAT/firewall constraints, and whether you have an internal proxy for egress?
- If you can share a small sample prompt + response distribution (token counts), Marissa can sketch batching/latency runs we'll target.

I've created a tentative calendar event (link below) — will convert to official invite once Alex confirms final attendee list.

Tentative event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234-redwood-poc

I'll also attach our PoC checklist to the calendar invite; Marissa will bring a short runbook for rollback/fallback during the migration.

Best,
Dev

Dev / Marissa —

Confirmed for Wed 09:30–11:00 PT. Samir will join for the infra section. A couple of specific agenda items we'd like to ensure you cover:
- KV cache warmup: expected behavior during traffic ramp and whether Redwood can pre-warm based on prefix caching
- Quantization paths: recommended 4-bit/8-bit quantization profiles that preserve our tuned weights
- Rollback: steps to redirect traffic back to EdgeScale in a failure scenario and associated SLA impacts

Also, could you point to any public docs or short notes on the rollback pattern you mentioned? That would help our SRE team before the call.

Thanks,
Alex
